scope: Proposition 2.4 (Projection on a flat torus) of the manuscript “Incompressible Box Transport and Finite Computation” (preprints/Incompressible-Box-Transport-and-Finite-Computation-October-6-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2505dc09d3f2c24b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let g be a smooth force on [0, ∞) × T3 L with zero spatial mean at each time. There is a unique smooth mean-zero potential ϕ satisfying ∆ϕ = div g. Put Qg = ∇ϕ and Pg = g − Qg. Then Pg is solenoidal and mean zero, and replacing (g, p) by (Pg, p − ϕ) preserves the velocity and the pressure normalization. Use normalized spatial measure, frequencies ξk = 2πk/L, and norms ∥G∥2 Hs = X k∈Z3 (1 + |ξk|2 )s | b G(k)|2 , ∥G∥Cr = max |β|≤r ∥∂β x G∥∞. For all integers h, r ≥ 0, at each time, max{∥∂h t Pg∥Cr , ∥∂h t Qg∥Cr } ≤ SL∥∂h t g∥Hr+2 , ∥∂h t ϕ∥Cr+1 ≤ SLdL∥∂h t g∥Hr+2 , (2) where SL = (1 + 52(L/(2π))4)1/2 and dL = (1 + (L/(2π))2)1/2. Uniform bounds, temporal L2 bounds on spatial suprema, and qualitative uniform decay of all mixed derivatives pass from g to Pg, Qg, ϕ. A quantitative envelope for time order h and output spatial order r passes to Pg, Qg through order r and to ϕ through order r + 1 when the input derivatives through spatial order r + 2 satisfy that envelope. The constants may depend on the derivative order. Periodicity and stationarity, including either property on a time tail, are preserved on their respective intervals. For computable L > 0, effective mixed-derivative evaluation and effective derivative bounds for g on finite time slabs give effective evaluation and such bounds for Pg, Qg, ϕ. Corresponding supplied global input bounds give effective global bounds in each assertion above.
